module.purpose: Provides authenticated, organization-aware server-side access control and feature loading for the settings layout before rendering its client component.
module.summary: This server layout authenticates the current user, redirects unauthenticated requests, retrieves organization feature flags and role permissions with short-lived caching, and passes the resulting settings capabilities to the client layout. It integrates session handling, multi-tenant organization context, feature repositories, permission checks, and role visibility controls.
module.businessContext:
This supports organization settings in a multi-tenant scheduling platform.
Failure can expose unauthorized settings or prevent legitimate users from managing role-related configuration.
functions: getTeamFeatures (~L19-28): Retrieves organization feature flags through a cached repository lookup.
getCachedResourcePermissions (~L30-37): Retrieves resource permissions through a cached permission service lookup.

sectionMap.name: Organization feature and permission loading
sectionMap.intent: Load organization features and role permissions concurrently when an organization exists.

sectionMap.name: Organization branch
sectionMap.intent: Skip organization-specific loading when no organization identifier is available.
branchOutcomes: orgId present: load features and role permissions
orgId absent: retain default feature and permission values

sectionMap.name: Feature availability and role permission evaluation
sectionMap.intent: Expose organization features and derive whether the user can read roles.
branchOutcomes: features truthy: store features and evaluate read-role permission
features falsy: retain null features and false role permission

sectionMap.name: Settings client rendering
sectionMap.intent: Render the client settings layout with props, features, and role permissions.

assumptions.description: The caller supplies props conforming to SettingsLayoutProps for forwarding to the client layout.
The server session may provide user.id and either user.profile.organizationId or user.org.id.
The Prisma client and permission and feature services are available when their lookups execute.
